newsitem.title: PERU: Siege boost over, Peru's Fujimori slips in polls.
newsitem.headline: Siege boost over, Peru's Fujimori slips in polls.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori's popularity fell back in February after approval for his handling of the hostage crisis temporarily broke his slide in the polls last month, a leading pollster said on Monday.

Analistas y Consultores -- the country's second-largest pollster -- published a survey showing the leader's approval rating slipped to 43 percent mid-February from 50 percent a month earlier. In December, his rating was also 43 percent.
The poll of 400 adults in Lima showed high approval of Fujimori's dealing with the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels holding 72 VIP hostages at the Japanese ambassador's home.

But his failure to reduce high levels of poverty and unemployment and his possible bid for a third term in office, which brought the president crashing in the polls last year, resurfaced as factors influencing the February results.

The latest poll coincides with a survey published over the weekend by a smaller pollster, Imasen, which showed Fujimori's popularity rating had fallen to 45 percent in early February from 50 percent in late December.

Since the start of the hostage crisis Dec. 17, Fujimori has refused to give in to rebel demands for the release of jailed comrades, but has consistently said he will look for a peaceful solution to the siege. In keeping with Peruvians' calls for dialogue with the MRTA, the president announced Sunday face-to-face talks between the government and rebels are due to start Tuesday.
